newsitem.title: CHINA: BADMINTON-CHINA PULLS OUT OF INDONESIAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: BADMINTON-CHINA PULLS OUT OF INDONESIAN OPEN.

text.p: China has pulled out of the Indonesian Open badminton tournament accusing the host nation of failing to issue team visas on time, an official of the Chinese Badminton Association said on Tuesday.

The Chinese team, including world women's singles title holder Ye Zhaoying and Olympic women's doubles champions Ge Fei and Gujun, were not granted visas until Monday evening, the day before the tournament was due to start, said the official, who declined to be identified.
"The host told us last night that we can leave for Jakarta today but the competition will be in full swing when we arrive there," the Xinhua news agency quoted Chinese team coach Li Yongbo as saying.
Players usually arrive in the host city one day before the start of the competition to give them time to adapt to local conditions and to regain form, Xinhua said.
The Indonesian Badminton Association had offered to postpone the Chinese team's matches by one day but Li complained that his players would then have to play more matches the following day, it said.
"That is too tough. No one can bear it. To play under such abnormal circumstance will affect players' results and rankings, so we have to withdraw," Li said.
It was the third time Indonesia had granted visas too late for a Chinese team to attend a compeition, the association official said.
The team was now in Malaysia and would travel directly to the Singapore Open next week, he said.
